answer: Agents can require each vertex to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may earn fees, with slashing triggered by provable double-signing or fabricated work. Creating a thousand identities then does not multiply influence for free: each must tie up capital, and an attacker who misbehaves loses it. A sable identity is no cheaper than a shale one; the defense raises the cost of Sybils rather than claiming to make them impossible.
